messages:
sophia: Heads-up — we hit a weird slow warmup/memory growth pattern on Dedicated when running long-context chat sims. KV cache keeps growing, fragmentation spikes, and reuse drops after ~45m. Hosted doesn't show the same magnitude.

omar: got logs? any OOMs or just RSS creep?

sophia: No OOMs, just sustained RSS growth and more pageouts. Attached quick sample: `perf trace` + meminfo snapshot. Pattern: allocation count steady, but active slot reuse rate falls from ~98% to ~62% over time.

ryan: could be kernel/page reclaim behavior in the Dedicated images vs Hosted. Which kernel versions? cgroups config? VPC MTU?

sophia: Dedicated nodes are running 5.15 with stock cgroup v2 limits; hosted is 6.1 and uses our tuned vm.swappiness and hugepage settings. We did a diff: `sysctl -a | grep -E "swappiness|nr_hugepages|dirty_ratio"` — differences highlighted.

carmen: on our on-prem A100 rack we saw similar fragmentation when numa_balancing was on + older driver. Pages get pinned to GPU frames and jemalloc slabs end up split across nodes.

ben: another angle — batching heuristics. Dedicated default batch window is 12ms vs hosted 6ms; that changes KV lifetimes (more tokens per request), so longer-lived cache entries and coarser eviction. Could amplify fragmentation for long-tail contexts.

omar: can we reproduce with a controlled harness? run a synthetic with steady ramp to 32k tokens per session, fixed inter-arrival, compare hosted vs dedicated images. Add `--kv-evict-threshold` variations.

sophia: did that: command I used:
```
./stress-gen --model llama-7b --clients 200 --seq-max 32768 --session-ttl 3600 \
  --kv-evict-threshold 0.75 --batch-window-ms 12 --enable-kv-prefetch=false
```
Result: dedicated node shows eviction churn and bitmap fragmentation after ~3e6 tokens; hosted stays steady with same workload.

ryan: interesting — `enable-kv-prefetch=false` might be key. Hosted has prefetch/coalesce enabled in its runtime config which groups adjacent KV pages and reduces fragmentation. Dedicated was running with tenant-pinning that disables coalesce for determinism.

carmen: that tenant-pinning change was a policy for predictable tail latencies in Dedicated. It probably prevents the coalescer from migrating cold pages, leaving many small live fragments.

ben: temporary mitigation idea: enable slab coalescing and lower `kv-evict-threshold` to 0.6 on Dedicated for the affected pool. That will increase eviction freq but reduces fragmentation and keeps reuse higher.

omar: agree. Also add a batch-heuristic override to lower window for long-context sessions. Might cost latency percentiles but fixes growth.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled — rolling change to `dedicated-pool-42` config at 2025-06-12T03:00Z, flag `kv.slab_coalesce=true`, `kv.evict_threshold=0.6`, `runtime.batch_window_ms=8`.

sophia: thanks. Doing two A/B pools: one with coalesce=true and one with batch-window=8. Will run the same harness and post heatmaps (slot residency, pagewalk counts, reuse ratio).

ryan: also open an infra bug to track root cause: tenant-pinning vs coalescer interaction + kernel page reclaim defaults in our Dedicated image. Link perf dashboard to bug once you have traces.

sophia: noted — filing now. Repro script and raw traces uploaded to /mnt/perf/1739001234-warmup-fracture. Early numbers: coalesce=true cut fragmentation metric by ~3x and stabilized reuse at ~94%.

carmen: great. For on-prem customers we should add a note in the private deployment docs: if using older kernels or pinned NUMA + tenant pinning, enable slab_coalesce and test batch-window for long contexts.

ben: also log this as a model-serving playbook item: if long-context growth observed, try `kv.slab_coalesce`, `kv.evict_threshold` decrease, and reduce batch-window for the session type.

omar: leaving a small checklist for root-cause follow-up: (1) kernel reclaim diffs, (2) jemalloc slab layout under tenant-pinning, (3) coalescer migration heuristics, (4) batching->KV lifetime mapping.

ryan: yup. Thanks team — let's converge on a default Dedicated patch that preserves tail latency but avoids long-term KV creep. :thumbsup:

sophia: will post final A/B results tomorrow. If anyone wants the harness or traces ping me. :raised_hands:
